=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Overall view

The package is materially seller-favourable. The Seller is seeking to combine a low general recovery regime with broad “data room/public records” disclosure, constructive buyer knowledge and blanket application of exclusions. That could leave Wattlebridge bearing known pre-Completion risks despite paying AUD 24m for a debt-free/cash-free company.

## Priority push-backs

### 1. Liability regime: do not apply one regime to all claims
**Seller position:** 20% cap (AUD 4.8m), 18-month survival, AUD 25,000 de minimis, AUD 250,000 deductible basket, and all limitations/exclusive remedies/non-reliance provisions applying to every claim.

**Buyer position:**
- Limit the 20% cap and 18-month period to ordinary business warranties only.
- Carve out, at minimum:
  - title, capacity and authority;
  - tax liabilities and tax covenant/indemnity;
  - fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment;
  - specific indemnities;
  - pre-Completion debt, leakage and transaction costs;
  - IP ownership/infringement and the Ironquay matter;
  - privacy/data-security incident liabilities.
- Seek a higher ordinary-warranty cap (commercially, at least 30% is a reasonable buyer ask in this risk profile), with separate caps or uncapped protection for the above categories.
- Title/capacity should be uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with substantially longer survival (typically six years or more).
- Tax protection should run through the relevant statutory limitation period, with an express tax covenant/indemnity—not merely ordinary tax warranties.
- For ordinary claims, seek a lower de minimis and an aggregate, first-dollar/tipping basket. At minimum, related claims should aggregate and the deductible should not apply to a claim once the threshold is crossed.
- Preserve claims for equitable relief, specific performance, fraud and non-excludable statutory rights. “Exclusive remedy” wording must not remove these rights.

### 2. Reject blanket data-room and public-records disclosure
**Seller position:** everything “contained or referred to” in the data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records is disclosed.

**Issue:** This shifts the burden of identifying and interpreting every adverse fact onto Buyer. It also permits Seller to rely on incomplete, scattered or ambiguous material.

**Buyer position:**
- General disclosure should not qualify warranties. Disclosure should be effective only if it is:
  - specifically identified against the relevant warranty;
  - in writing;
  - fair, clear and sufficiently detailed as to nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences; and
  - contained in an agreed, indexed disclosure bundle frozen at signing.
- Delete disclosure by reference to “publicly searchable” records and material merely “referred to” in the data room.
- Require a data-room index, date-stamped export and confirmation that the disclosed material is complete and unaltered.
- A disclosure should not protect Seller against a matter it knew was materially incomplete or misleading.

### 3. Remove constructive buyer-knowledge exclusion
**Seller position:** no claim for anything known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters “discoverable” from the data room or public records.

**Buyer position:** Limit this, if accepted at all, to the actual knowledge of named senior Wattlebridge deal personnel as at signing, obtained from a written disclosure that fairly disclosed the matter. Do not impute adviser knowledge, junior-team knowledge, constructive knowledge, or matters that could have been discovered through diligence.

## Known transaction risks

### 4. Bluefen: make effective consent a Completion condition
Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue. The data room apparently lacks final consent and evidence that clause 11.3 conditions have been met.

**Push back:**
- The condition must require a final, unconditional written consent from Bluefen and satisfaction or waiver by Bluefen of every condition to that consent.
- Consent must be effective at Completion and must not permit termination, price reduction, changed commercial terms or other adverse action.
- “Seller will use reasonable endeavours” is insufficient for a customer representing 30% of revenue.
- If consent is not obtained by the long-stop date, Buyer should be able to terminate without liability, or elect a negotiated price reduction/escrow arrangement.

### 5. Riverlark debt/security: repay and release at Completion, not later
The facility has approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding and no final security discharge is available.

**Push back:**
- Completion must occur only against simultaneous repayment, irrevocable discharge/release of all Riverlark security, guarantees and claims, and delivery of release documents in agreed form.
- The repayment must be shown as a Seller-funded deduction in the agreed funds flow; it cannot become Company debt after a purported debt-free/cash-free Completion.
- Include all interest, break costs, fees, contingent liabilities and costs of discharge within “Debt.”
- Do not accept a release “following Completion.”

### 6. Completion bonuses: treat as Seller liability/leakage
DD-005 records AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, excluded from the funds flow, with unknown payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

**Push back:**
- Seller should pay these before Completion, or the full amount plus all payroll tax, super, leave effects and other on-costs should be deducted from price and separately itemised.
- Define these amounts as debt, transaction costs or prohibited leakage, as appropriate.
- Obtain a schedule of recipients, terms, payment date, conditions and total employer cost.
- Wattlebridge should not inherit a Completion-triggered liability that economically benefits Seller.

### 7. Ironquay IP: broaden the specific indemnity
The current proposal only covers a particular SOW3 payment. The disclosed position suggests AUD 180,000 remains open and the IP transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.

**Push back:**
- Require a specific indemnity for all loss arising from Ironquay and the SOWs, including fees, interest, enforcement costs, failure of assignment, chain-of-title defects, IP infringement claims, replacement/development costs and diminution in value.
- The indemnity should not be subject to the general cap, basket or 18-month period.
- Require before Completion: payment evidence, an executed confirmatory IP assignment, waiver/release from Ironquay, and confirmation that the Company owns all relevant project materials free of security interests and third-party claims.
- This is not adequately addressed by an indemnity limited to one invoice.

### 8. Export/privacy incident: require facts, remediation and protection
The incident may involve approximately 1,240 records, with uncertainty about access, scope and notification obligations.

**Push back:**
- Require a completed forensic investigation before Completion, including access logs, confirmed data scope, recipient actions, containment and deletion evidence.
- Require Seller to bear all pre-Completion incident costs and liabilities, including investigation, legal advice, notification, remediation, regulator engagement, customer communications and claims.
- Obtain a specific indemnity outside general limitations.
- Require a pre-Completion privacy/data-security warranty and a covenant to notify Buyer immediately of developments.
- If material access, notification obligations, regulatory action or customer impact emerges, Buyer should have a termination or other negotiated remedy.

## Other material points

### 9. Tax and IP cannot sit solely in the general regime
Tax and core IP are central value risks in an analytics business.

**Push back:**
- Include a stand-alone tax covenant/indemnity for all pre-Completion tax, with statutory-period survival.
- Ensure tax covers payroll tax and other employment on-costs on the bonuses.
- Obtain robust IP ownership, non-infringement, open-source, contractor-assignment and data-rights warranties, with suitable survival and cap treatment.

### 10. Supplier renewals: restrict pre-Completion commitments
The three Sandbar renewals total AUD 330,000. Their term, termination rights, accrual status and ordinary-course character remain unclear.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the complete agreements and renewal notices.
- Require Seller not to renew, amend, prepay or enter material supplier commitments without Buyer consent between signing and Completion.
- If unavoidable, require price adjustment, deduction or express Buyer approval. “Ordinary course” should not itself resolve whether these are liabilities or commitments that Buyer is accepting.

### 11. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the actual contractual result
The disclosures are framed defensively: they say a notification obligation is not necessarily consent, and an assignment restriction is not necessarily triggered by a share sale.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the complete operative agreements and a Seller legal/factual confirmation of whether notice or consent is required.
- Require all required notices/consents to be delivered before Completion and cover any resulting fees or claims.
- Do not rely on the Seller’s characterisation of the clauses.

### 12. Title evidence is insufficient by itself
A share register showing Seller as holder is useful but does not alone establish unencumbered title, authority, no options, no third-party claims, or valid transfer mechanics.

**Push back:**
- Require title and capacity warranties, free from general limitations.
- Obtain executed transfers, original share certificates or indemnities, board approvals, register updates, ASIC compliance evidence, and releases of any share security or third-party rights.
- Confirm no options, warrants, convertibles, pre-emption rights, drag/tag rights or shareholder claims.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. **Do not accept** the proposed universal cap, 18-month period, blanket disclosure, constructive-knowledge or all-claims exclusion provisions.  
2. **Make Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment/security release hard Completion conditions.**  
3. **Treat the bonuses, Riverlark debt and related costs as Seller-funded amounts in the funds flow.**  
4. **Require uncapped or separately capped, longer-duration protection** for title, tax, fraud, IP/Ironquay, known privacy incident, debt/leakage and specific indemnities.  
5. **Replace generic disclosure with a closed, specific and fair disclosure standard.**  
6. **Obtain missing evidence before signing/Completion**, particularly Bluefen consent, Riverlark releases, Ironquay title/payment documents, privacy investigation results and supplier/lease/Mossvale contractual analysis.
